<result>## Investigation Findings — Mobile Swipe Not Paging the Gallery

I read both components (and their `.css.ts` files) in full, plus `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, `zimmSlideIndicator`, `zimmProductCardContent`, `globalStyles.ts`, git history, both test files, e2e coverage, and `playwright.config.js`. Findings below map to your 7 numbered checks, then a ranked-theory synthesis.

### 1–2. The current mechanism (confirmed, nothing new vs. your brief)

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`:
- `scrollContainerRef` attached at line 229, on the div styled by `styles.scrollContainer` (line 230).
- Only handler on that div is `onKeyDown={handleScrollContainerKeyDown}` (line 235) — ArrowLeft/ArrowRight only (lines 191–195). No `onTouchStart`/`onPointerDown`/`onClick` anywhere on the container or its ancestors.
- `scrollend` listener (lines 203–215) only *reads* `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth` to update the indicator — never calls `preventDefault`, never blocks anything.
- `badge`/`close`/`carousel`/`indicatorWrapper` (lines 274–317) are DOM **siblings** of `scrollContainer`, not children of it.

`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`:
- `scrollContainer` (lines 65–84): `display:flex, width:'100%', overflowX:'auto', scrollSnapType:'x mandatory', WebkitOverflowScrolling:'touch', scrollbarWidth:'none'` + `_focusVisible`. **No `position`, no `height`, no `touchAction` key at all.**
- `slide` (lines 86–97): `position:'relative', flex:'0 0 100%', width:'100%', aspectRatio:'2 / 3', scrollSnapAlign:'start', overflow:'hidden'`. No `transform`/`will-change`.
- `carousel` (lines 172–195): `position:'absolute', transform:'translateY(-50%)', display:'none'` (unconditional at this file's level), `pointerEvents:'none'` (wrapper, line 194) / `'auto'` (arrowButton, line 207). Reveal now lives *only* in the organism recipe's `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` — which never matches a touchscreen, so on a real phone this part is never rendered/painted at all (irrelevant to the bug on mobile).
- `indicatorWrapper` (lines 217–226): `position:absolute, left:0, right:0, bottom:0`, no explicit height — sized to `ZimmSlideIndicator`'s own 1px hairline (`zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:32`, `height: var(--zimm-scale-025)`). Too small to be a plausible invisible hit-area over the image. Ruled out.

**`touch-action`**: repo-wide `grep -rniE "touch-action|touchAction"` across every `.ts/.tsx/.scss/.css` (excluding node_modules) returns **zero hits**. It is not set anywhere — not in this component family, not in `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` (read in full — only typography/grid/form/focus utility classes, nothing touch-related), not in any Chakra recipe. This rules out the classic "`touch-action: pan-y`/`none` on an ancestor" cause entirely.

### 3. Transform/stacking-context and container sizing

- No `transform`/`will-change` on `scrollContainer` or `slide` — only `carousel` (a sibling, `display:none` on touch) has `transform`, and it doesn't nest inside `scrollContainer`, so it can't break scroll-snap there.
- `scrollContainer` has no explicit height/width beyond `width:'100%'`; height is derived from `slide`'s `aspectRatio` via flex layout — nothing structurally suspicious, and `aspect-ratio` is within this project's stated browserslist (iOS ≥ 17, Android ≥ 14, per `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own docblock). I found no code-level evidence of a 0-width-collapse bug; this would need a live/Playwright render to fully exclude, but nothing points at it.

### 4. The actual finding: whole-card stretched-link overlay sits on top of the gallery, untested for this exact surface

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts:219-223`:
```
[`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] a::after`]: {
  content: '""',
  position: 'absolute',
  inset: 0,
},
```
This targets the real `<a>` (`ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink)`, defined `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:39`, rendered at line 210 inside `data-card-slot="content"` at line 208). I verified independently (not just trusting the docblock) that neither `ZimmProductCardContent`'s `root`, `nameRow`, nor `nameLink` sets `position` anywhere — `grep -n position zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` returns **zero matches**. So the `position:absolute; inset:0` containing block for this `::after` resolves to the nearest ancestor that *does* set `position`, which is the **organism root** (`zimmProductCard.css.ts:213`, `position:'relative'`), not `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own box. The file's own docblock (lines 59–61) confirms this explicitly: *"`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root` IS `position: relative`, but Media is a sibling of Content under this organism's root, never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain."* Net effect: **the invisible overlay is sized to the entire card — image area and text area both** — not just the name row.

Critically, this overlay carries **no `z-index`, deliberately** (docblock lines 194–199; proven by the recipe's own test, `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx:507-514`, which asserts `hasOwnProperty(after,'zIndex') === false`). The recipe then explicitly lifts exactly three things above it, and only three, `zimmProductCard.css.ts:240-253`:
```
[`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.close}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },          // line 240-242
[`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },       // line 247-249
[`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {              // line 250-253
  position: 'relative', zIndex: 1,
},
```
The docblock's own reasoning for why (lines 62–64): *"a z-index higher than the overlay's own (left unset), **or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first**."* This is the codebase itself stating, in writing, that anything not on this list gets its clicks intercepted by the overlay.

There is **no equivalent lift for `[data-card-slot="media"]`, `scrollContainer`, or `slide`** — confirmed via `grep -n "CARD_SLOT.media"` on `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: zero matches. `scrollContainer` doesn't even carry a `data-card-slot` attribute (only Media's outermost `root` does, `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:227`). `scrollContainer` itself is `position:static` (no `position` key at all, confirmed above), and `slide` is `position:relative` with `z-index:auto` — un-lifted.

Because `ZimmProductCardMedia` renders **before** `ZimmProductCardContent` in the organism (`zimmProductCard/index.tsx:441-450` then `451-470`), and neither Media's root nor the organism's own root establishes a real stacking context (`position:relative` with `z-index:auto` doesn't create one per CSS2.1 — only a set z-index, transform, opacity<1, filter, or isolation would), the `<a>::after` (positioned, z-index:auto) and `scrollContainer`/`slide` end up compared in the same ancestor stacking context, where a positioned element always paints above non-positioned in-flow content, and among same-level positioned/auto elements the later one in DOM order (Content) wins. Either way the result is the same: **the overlay paints, and therefore hit-tests, on top of the whole image/gallery region.**

This is exactly the same bug *class* this codebase has already caught and fixed once — for the desktop arrow buttons (Fix 3, `zimmProductCard.css.ts` docblock lines 84–101, and `index.test.tsx:525-539` / `843-866`): a `transform`-induced stacking context trapped the arrows' own z-index so real clicks landed on the overlay "despite passing every jsdom test," only caught by "the manual real-browser check performed after the round-2 Scorer PASS." That audit pass evidently covered `close`/`carousel`/content buttons (click targets) but was never extended to the touch/swipe gesture on the image itself.

The test suite's own **"KNOWN LIMITATION"** docblock (`zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx:312-328`) states this gap explicitly and by name:
> *"jsdom performs no real layout, paint, or hit-testing (no CSS cascade resolution, no stacking-context/z-index comparison, no geometry at all)... going from 'the right CSS values exist' to 'a real browser click lands on the right element' is exactly the gap a real-browser (Playwright or manual) check is for."*

No test anywhere — jsdom or Playwright — exercises a click/touch/drag on `scrollContainer`/`slide`/the image itself to prove it isn't shadowed by this overlay. The one organism test that touches the carousel (`index.test.tsx:338`, "the carousel arrows fire independently of the name-link overlay") only clicks the arrow *buttons* (already lifted), never the image region.

Ancestor `onClick`/`onTouchStart`/`onPointerDown` with `preventDefault`: none found anywhere in the ancestor chain (`grep` across `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` and the organism `index.tsx` shows only ordinary `onClick` on the bag and notify-me buttons — unrelated to the swipe path).

`pointer-events`: only two occurrences in the whole `ui-kits` tree, both already read — `carousel` wrapper `pointerEvents:'none'` / `arrowButton` `'auto'` (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:194,207`) — both irrelevant on touch since `carousel` isn't rendered there.

### 5–7. Git history, tests, e2e — corroborating the theory

- Every commit touching these three files (`219d0a1` → `548b9d7`, ~11 commits) was inspected in full (subject + body). Every real-device-caught bug is described as found via **"manual real-browser check," "live-browser testing,"** or **"live Figma"** — one (`72ee2a9`) explicitly mentions a **Storybook**-specific fix ("Storybook placeholder-fill colour correction... dark fills were masking overlays in Storybook"). **None of the ~11 commits mention "touch," "swipe," "mobile device," or a Playwright/mobile run.** The verification method that did catch stacking bugs (Fix 1: close button knocked out of position; Fix 3: carousel arrows unclickable) was demonstrably desktop-mouse-click testing, not touch-drag testing.
- `ZimmProductCard` is **not yet consumed by any page/grid** — `grep` for consumers outside its own folder only finds `zimmProductCardShared.ts` and the theme recipe registry (`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:33-35,70-72`). The only place it currently renders anywhere is its own `index.stories.tsx` and its Vitest suite. So any "real mobile device" check the developer did was necessarily against **Storybook's own iframe render of this isolated organism** — which doesn't add or remove any ancestor overlay (no page-level grid wrapper exists yet to introduce a *different* bug), so it reproduces the exact same stretched-link-over-gallery DOM/CSS. This actually reinforces the theory rather than complicating it: the bug is fully self-contained inside these two components today.
- `e2e/tests/zimm/` contains only `homepage/SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js`, `homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js`, and `homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js` — **nothing referencing `zimmProductCard`/`zimmProductCardMedia` at all.**
- `playwright.config.js:64-68` **does** define a `mobile-chrome` project (`devices['Pixel 5']`) and the repo already has a mobile-spec-folder precedent (`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/`) — so the infrastructure to catch this with a real touch-emulated Playwright run exists, it has simply never been pointed at this component. Nothing in the codebase uses `page.touchscreen` or any swipe/drag simulation for this gallery.
- `zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` only exercises: `scrollTo` call shape via click on arrow buttons (lines 146–175), the `scrollend`→indicator wiring via a synthetic `Event('scrollend')` (lines 384–409), and keyboard ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (lines 411–429). **No touch/pointer/drag simulation exists anywhere in this file** — confirmed via `grep -n "touch\|swipe\|scroll"`.

### Ranked theories

1. **(Primary, strongly evidenced)** The organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay (`zimmProductCard.css.ts:219-223`, selector `[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`) is sized via `inset:0` to the entire card (image + text), carries no `pointer-events:none` and no `z-index`, and — unlike `close`/`carousel`/content buttons (`zimmProductCard.css.ts:240-253`) — has no corresponding lift for `media`/`scrollContainer`/`slide`. A touchstart landing on the image resolves to this overlay's owning `<a>` element (a sibling subtree of Media, never an ancestor of `scrollContainer`), so the browser's native scroll-gesture recognizer never engages `scrollContainer` at all — no scroll ever happens, `scrollend` never fires, and the indicator (purely state/prop-driven) sits there correctly rendered but never updates. This is the identical bug *class* already caught once for the desktop arrows (Fix 3) via manual real-browser testing that was never extended to the swipe surface — a gap the test suite's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock (`index.test.tsx:312-328`) names directly, and git history confirms no touch-specific verification (Playwright mobile or real device) was ever performed on this component.
2. **(Weak, unconfirmed, would need a live render to fully exclude)** Some real-device-only sizing quirk collapsing `scrollContainer`'s real scrollable width to ~0 despite working in Storybook/desktop — no supporting code evidence found (no explicit height, no transform, no touch-action interfering); ranked low-confidence.
3. **(Ruled out)** `touch-action` blocking horizontal panning — zero occurrences repo-wide.
4. **(Ruled out on real mobile)** Carousel `transform`-induced stacking context intercepting the swipe — `carousel` is `display:none` on any real touchscreen (gated behind `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` + organism `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`, which never matches a touch-only pointer), so it isn't even in the paint tree on mobile; only relevant as precedent for the same bug pattern.
5. **(Ruled out)** Ancestor `onClick`/`onTouchStart`/`onPointerDown` calling `preventDefault` — none exist in the ancestor chain besides the keyboard-only handler on the scroll container itself.

Files most relevant to cite in a fix plan: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts:219-223` (the overlay) and `:240-253` (the existing lift pattern to extend), `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:227-236` (root/scrollContainer, no `data-card-slot` on `scrollContainer` itself to target), and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx:312-328` (the limitation this bug fell through).</result>

attachment.planContent:
# Live ZimmProductCard homepage demo (temporary, throwaway branch + draft PR)

## Context

PR #85 (SFCC-236, `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`, still open against `develop`)
built the shared `ZimmProductCard` component family but deliberately shipped no page wiring — it's
Storybook-only today. Marcel wants to demonstrate it live, using real SFCC product data, on the
homepage, via a throwaway branch that triggers this repo's ephemeral MRT preview environment so
stakeholders can see it in a real browser. Confirmed with him directly: **add-to-bag must be fully
real** (the actual basket mutation, not simulated), and **this is temporary** — built to show live
once, then the branch/PR gets discarded, not merged.

Four rounds of codebase research this session (git history, live workflow YAML, the real PDP
add-to-cart chain, and a direct read of the current home page) established every fact this plan
relies on — cited inline below rather than re-derived.

## Approach

### 1. Branch

```bash
git checkout -b feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo   # from the current tip of feature/SFCC-236_..., do NOT rebase onto develop
```

Branched from SFCC-236's own tip deliberately — `ZimmProductCard` has to already exist for this to
demo anything. Name deliberately carries **no `SFCC-###` pattern anywhere** (not in the branch name,
PR title, or PR body): `.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` greps the PR title+body+branch
name for `SFCC-[0-9]+` to decide whether to run BrowserStack/Zephyr and possibly auto-file a Jira
defect on failure — this PR has no real story behind it, so guaranteeing that detection finds nothing
is the reliable way to keep it a no-op.

`deploy-preview.yml` triggers on `push` to any `feature/**` branch (no PR needed, no path filter) —
pushing this branch is what spins up the MRT preview; the PR is only for the auto-posted preview-URL
comment and isn't required for the environment to exist.

### 2. New files — data fetching + mapping

**`overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts`** (new, pure functions, no React/react-intl
import — mirrors `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`'s established shape: a
formatter injected as a parameter rather than importing `useIntl` itself).

- `resolveDemoVariant(hit)` — picks the first orderable variant (else `variants[0]`, else the master
  hit itself) and returns its `productId`/`price`/colour-code/size-code.
- `resolveAttributeName(hit, attributeId, code)` — cross-references a variation code (`variationValues`
  only holds codes, e.g. `{color: 'BLACK'}`) against `variationAttributes[].values[].name` for the
  human-readable label.
- `selectLiveProductCardBase(hit, formatPrice)` — builds the shared base props every card instance
  starts from: `href` (via base's `productUrlBuilder`), `name`, `primaryImage`/`hoverImage`/`images`
  (via base's real `filterImageGroups` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils`,
  confirmed exported — `viewType: 'medium'`, filtered by the resolved colour), `currentPrice`
  (`formatPrice(variant.price, hit.currency)`, skipped entirely if either is missing rather than
  guessing a fallback currency). `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is a required, non-empty field
  (unlike base `ProductTile`'s own deliberately-decorative `alt: ''` convention) — synthesize from
  `name` + resolved colour when SFCC's own `image.alt` is blank.
- `buildSizeChipValues(hit)` — maps the `'size'` variation attribute's values to `ZimmSizeChipValue[]`
  (`isDisabled` from `orderable === false`). **Not independently verified this session** that `'size'`
  is this org's real attribute id (`'color'` is already an established literal elsewhere in this
  codebase; no equivalent size constant exists yet since nothing currently consumes real size data) —
  confirm against one real logged response during implementation; the function degrades to an empty
  array rather than throwing if the id is wrong.
- `pickDemoHit(hits)` — from the ~10 hits `useProductSearch` returns, prefers one with ≥2 images AND
  ≥2 sizes (so the multi-image and size-chip states both have real content), falls back to ≥1 image,
  falls back to `hits[0]`.

**`overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx`** (new) — the container:
- Calls `useProductSearch` with the **identical parameters** `HomepageContent` already uses
  (`HOME_SHOP_PRODUCTS_CATEGORY_ID`/`HOME_SHOP_PRODUCTS_LIMIT`, both real imports from
  `overrides/app/constants`) — React Query dedupes this against the existing call, zero extra network
  cost, and it's the one query in this repo already proven to return real hits from the live dev org.
  No separate `useProduct` call — `ProductSearchHit` already carries everything needed once
  `expand: ['variations','prices','images']` is requested, which it already is.
- Owns the real add-to-bag mutation (§4), the demo-only `onNotifyMe`/`onRemove` toasts, and renders
  the 11 card instances (§3), each wrapped in a page-local size-selection helper (§5).

### 3. Eleven card instances — one real product's data reused, per-instance prop overrides for the rest

**Decision: reuse ONE real product's data as the shared base, override only the specific prop(s)
needed per state** — the same pattern `index.stories.tsx` itself already uses (`{...Default.args,
<override>}`), just with a real fetched product substituted for the hand-authored SVG fixture.
Justified because states like `WithSalePrice`/`OneSize`/`LoadingPrice` can never be "naturally
occurring" from a plain search hit regardless of which product is picked (a search hit has no clean
"is this actually on sale" signal the way the PDP's own `getPriceData` pipeline does), so the override
mechanism is required either way — and one real SKU flowing through every "Add to bag" click keeps
the live basket verification trivial (one line item, quantity increments) during the demo itself.

| # | Label | `variation` | Override vs. shared base | Demonstrates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Default (PLP) | `plp` | none | baseline: real image/price, interactive size chips, real add-to-bag |
| 2 | PLP — Out of stock | `plp` | `isUnavailable: true`, `onNotifyMe` (demo toast) | forced override — real product presumably orderable |
| 3 | Home | `home` | none (still passes `badge`/`hoverImage`) | proves `VARIATION_CONFIG` suppresses both on Home even when supplied |
| 4 | Home — Out of stock | `home` | `isUnavailable: true`, `onNotifyMe` | Home's additive (not swap) unavailable treatment |
| 5 | Wishlist | `wishlist` | resolved `colour`/`size`, `onRemove` (demo toast), real add-to-bag | working size setting + real add-to-bag on a 2nd variation |
| 6 | Wishlist — Out of stock | `wishlist` | `isUnavailable: true`, `onNotifyMe` | Wishlist's narrower mobile bag-hide rule |
| 7 | Single image | `plp` | `hoverImage`/`images` forced `undefined` | single-image path, paired against #8 off the same product |
| 8 | Multiple images | `plp` | real `images` array (needs `pickDemoHit` to have found ≥2 images) | gallery + arrows + slide indicator |
| 9 | With sale price | `plp` | `originalPrice` forced (synthetic, e.g. price × 1.4) | Was/Now treatment |
| 10 | One size | `plp` | `sizeChipValues: [{value:'os', label:'One size'}]`; **not** wrapped in the size-selection helper | non-interactive single-size branch |
| 11 | Loading price | `plp` | `currentPrice: undefined, isPriceLoading: true` | price-loading placeholder |

Maps directly onto Marcel's own list: "working size setting" → #1/#5; "adding to bag/cart" → real
`onAddToBag` on every plp/wishlist instance (all except #3/#4 — `ZimmProductCard`'s `home` variation
has **no** `onAddToBag`/bag button at all, `VARIATION_CONFIG.home.showBag: false` by original,
already-shipped AC-driven design, confirmed in `index.tsx`); "multiple images" → #8; "change image on
hover" → #1's hover-swap pair; "all the variants and states" → 1:1 with the 11 stories already in
`organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx`.

Render as a small array of `{label, cardProps}` mapped to JSX rather than 11 hand-written blocks.

### 4. Real add-to-bag — mirrors the PDP's actual chain, stripped to the load-bearing line

```ts
import { useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper as useShopperBasketsMutationHelper } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';

const { addItemToNewOrExistingBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutationHelper();
const showToast = useToast();

const handleAddToBag = async () => {
  if (!demoProduct) return;
  try {
    await addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([
      { productId: demoProduct.variantProductId, price: demoProduct.variantPrice, quantity: 1 },
    ]);
    showToast({ title: 'Added to bag', status: 'success' });
  } catch (error) {
    showToast({ title: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Could not add to bag', status: 'error' });
  }
};
```

This is `handleAddToCart` (`product-detail/index.tsx:507-598`) with every BOPIS/multiship/analytics
concern removed — what's left is the same one load-bearing line the real PDP uses,
`await addItemToNewOrExistingBasket(productItems)`, in the same try/catch → toast shape already
established there for the failure path. `addItemToNewOrExistingBasket` handles "no basket yet"
internally (creates one) — no separate branch needed. Guest-safe with no extra handling: the SDK's
own `auth.ready()` transparently resolves a guest SLAS session under every mutation call. Success
toast has no real-PDP precedent (the real flow opens a modal instead) — modeled on the PDP's own
wishlist-add success toast instead, the closest existing plain-toast-on-success precedent in this
codebase. One shared `handleAddToBag` passed to every plp/wishlist instance — correct, not a
simplification, since they all share the same real variant.

`onNotifyMe`/`onRemove` stay demo-only toasts (`status: 'info'`) — Marcel's "fully real" decision was
scoped to add-to-bag specifically; no notify-me or wishlist-remove mutation exists anywhere in this
codebase to wire them to.

**Known, un-fixed gap, flagged not patched**: `ZimmProductCardContent`'s bag button has no
loading-spinner slot at all (its only lever is `isUnavailable`) — a slow request shows no in-button
pending state. This is a real limitation of the shared component itself; fixing it is out of scope
for a throwaway demo page (would be scope creep onto a broadly-consumed Tier-3 component) — one line
in the PR body, not a code change.

### 5. Working size selection

A page-local, unexported helper in `liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx`, adapted from
`index.stories.tsx`'s own `LiveSizeSelectionCard` (same narrowing reasoning that file already
documents: attaching `selectedSizeChipValue`/`onSizeChipSelect` onto an *unnarrowed* prop spread
fails `tsc` on the `home` union branch, so narrow via the `variation` discriminant first):

```tsx
const DemoSizeSelectableCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
  const [selectedSizeChipValue, setSelectedSizeChipValue] = useState<string | undefined>(() =>
    props.variation === 'plp' || props.variation === 'wishlist' ? props.selectedSizeChipValue : undefined,
  );
  const isSizeChipVariation = props.variation === 'plp' || props.variation === 'wishlist';
  const handleSizeChipSelect = (value: string) => {
    setSelectedSizeChipValue(value);
    (isSizeChipVariation ? props.onSizeChipSelect : undefined)?.(value);
  };
  const propsWithLiveSelection: ZimmProductCardProps = isSizeChipVariation
    ? { ...props, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect: handleSizeChipSelect }
    : props;
  return <ZimmProductCard {...propsWithLiveSelection} />;
};
```

Wraps every plp/wishlist instance except #10 (`OneSize` renders a non-interactive `<span>` — nothing
to select, same reason the story file skips wrapping its own `OneSize`). Each mount owns an
independent `useState`, so the 8 or so instances never cross-contaminate selection state.

### 6. Wiring into the homepage — corrected placement, verified by reading the real file

**`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`'s existing `HomepageContent` (the current "Shop Products"
section) is itself still gated behind `HomeNormal`'s `if (!homepageContent) return null` check** —
confirmed by reading the file directly, not assumed. On a genuinely blank homepage (no published
Contentful `homepage` entry — the exact state Marcel described), `HomeNormal` returns `null` *before*
ever reaching `HomepageContent`, so mounting the new demo section inside `HomepageContent` (as
originally sketched) would make it invisible on precisely the page state this is meant to fill.

**Correct placement: directly in the top-level `Home` component, unconditional, before the
Contentful-gated branch** — so it always renders regardless of CMS state or preview mode:

```tsx
// index.tsx — two additions only
import { LiveProductCardDemoSection } from './liveProductCardDemoSection';
// ...
const Home = () => {
  const { search } = useLocation();
  const entryId = new URLSearchParams(search).get('entry');
  return (
    <Box data-testid="home-page">
      <Seo .../>
      <LiveProductCardDemoSection />
      {entryId ? <HomePreviewContent entryId={entryId} /> : <HomeNormal />}
    </Box>
  );
};
```

No change to `HomepageContent`/`HomeNormal`/`HomePreviewContent`/`routes.tsx` at all. This crosses
zero protection tiers — `overrides/app/pages/home/` is in neither `frozenFiles.md` (Tier 1) nor
`protectedFiles.md` (Tier 2). (One pre-existing doc contradiction worth a passing mention, not a
blocker: CODEOWNERS routes this path to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`, while `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
also separately claims it — real, pre-existing drift, not something this throwaway demo should
resolve.)

### 7. PR — draft, targeting `develop`, explicitly marked throwaway

```bash
git push -u origin feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo

gh pr create --draft --base develop \
  --title "demo(home): live ZimmProductCard states on homepage — temporary, do not merge" \
  --body "<see below>"
```

PR body opens with a bold **"THROWAWAY DEMO — DO NOT MERGE"** callout explaining its purpose (trigger
the MRT preview, show PR #85's component live against real SFCC data), states it'll be closed and its
branch deleted once the demo is done (`teardown-preview.yml` tears the preview down on either event),
and asks reviewers/CodeRabbit not to spend real review time on it. Lists the 3 changed files, how to
test-drive it (open the preview URL Deploy Preview posts, hover/click/add-to-bag), notes no Tier 1/2
files are touched, and explicitly checks "Testing: intentionally skipped" / "Accessibility: not
assessed" with the one-line reason each (throwaway, not a production surface) rather than silently
omitting those sections.

**Cleanup after the demo**: `gh pr close` + `git push origin --delete feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`
— either alone triggers `teardown-preview.yml`.

## Known gaps / simplifications (surfaced, not silent)

- Bag button has no loading-spinner slot (§4) — not fixed, shared-component scope creep.
- `onNotifyMe`/`onRemove` are demo-only toasts, not real mutations — only add-to-bag was required to
  be real.
- `WithSalePrice`'s `originalPrice` is always synthetic — no clean "on promotion" signal exists on a
  plain search hit.
- The `'size'` variation-attribute id is assumed, not verified against a live response yet — confirm
  during implementation.
- No Storybook/Vitest coverage for the new mapper/section, no i18n `defineMessages` for the new
  demo-only copy — accepted, matches the confirmed throwaway framing.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Manual smoke test against Marcel's own local dev server (`localhost:3000`, already running) —
   this is the first real chance to confirm `useProductSearch` actually returns hits and the `'size'`
   attribute-id guess is correct, since a plain `curl` against the SSR HTML can't see this (confirmed
   this session: the product-search section's data is client-fetched post-hydration, invisible to a
   non-JS request). Check: all 11 states render with real data, hover swap works on #1, size chips
   select on #1/#5, "Add to bag" on at least one instance produces a real toast and a real new/updated
   basket line item.
3. Push, confirm `deploy-preview.yml` runs and the PR comment posts a real preview hostname.
4. Open the preview URL in a real browser and repeat step 2's checks against the deployed build, not
   just localhost.

**Explicit stop points, not implied by plan approval alone**: this plan's own git-push and
`gh pr create` steps (§1, §7) are outward-facing actions — implement and verify the code first, then
pause for a separate, explicit go before pushing or opening the PR, matching this session's standing
practice for every prior push/PR/commit in this build.

skills.name: zimmerMANNPostBuild
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPostBuild

Marcel's own senior dev. Nothing built here — this skill judges what was built, writes what goes
public, and holds the conversation with CodeRabbit and the reviewer.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Input:** `Final wrap-up pass for SFCC-236 (Product Card Shared Component) before opening the PR. HEAD is now at 4740dd5, 5 commits past Round 9's last audit (72ee2a9 arrows hover-gating fix, 983bddf :has(:focus-visible) stuck-open-hover fix, 0748af3 was/now sale price story for ProductCardContent, 02a3203 ZimmProductCard stories consolidation — nodeCoverage/ deleted, 11 stories in one file, 4740dd5 slide-indicator docblock clarification). Explicit checks requested by the developer for this round:
- Check against the build plan (~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md) — confirm the shipped state still matches, flag any drift.
- Check the JIRA ticket (SFCC-236) details, ACs, and comment thread directly — not just prior session summaries of them.
- Check the designs: design spec accuracy, tokens, etc., via the live Figma design nodes (not cached descriptions).
- Run visual checks (Storybook, real rendering).
- Run accessibility checks (keyboard nav, screen reader/ARIA correctness, WCAG 2.2 AA per AGENTS.md).
This is intended to be the final round before the PR is opened — treat it as a genuinely fresh, thorough audit, not a diff-only check of the 5 recent commits.` — a Jira key. Reads three files under
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- **`handoff.md`** — Build's record: steps, commits, Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers,
  UNIFORM findings, what went unverified
- **`plan.md`** — what was meant to be built
- **`findings.md`** — the gate table, with its 🟡 CLARIFY assumptions

If `handoff.md` is missing, Build either did not finish or ran before this was written. Say so and
reconstruct what you can from the branch's commits — but flag the audit as partial, because the
Scorer verdicts and UNIFORM findings are not recoverable from git.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get a five-agent sweep. Honour the scale the
plan chose. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — audit against both artefacts

Two documents, two different questions. Neither is covered by the loop that just ran.

### `findings.md` — did the gate hold?

Walk every row. For each:

- **🔴 BLOCKED** — was it resolved before Build started, and by what?
- **🟡 CLARIFY** — this is the one that matters. Each of these carried a **stated assumption** into
  the plan. **Did that assumption actually hold once the code existed?** Nothing else in the chain
  revisits them. An assumption that turned out wrong mid-build, that nobody went back to, is the
  most likely thing to reach the PR unnoticed.
- **🔵 NOTE** — still true? A note that has become a defect is a finding.

### `plan.md` — did the build deliver?

- Every step shipped what it promised, with its Scorer verdict.
- The diff matches the file manifest. Anything in the diff that isn't in the manifest is a scope
  finding — even if it looks correct.
- Every file's tier is what the plan said it was.
- **Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.** Never a finding.

Use `zm-orchestrator` for the manifest-versus-diff conformance pass. It already does exactly this
judgement at step scope.

---

## Phase 2 — the whole-feature sweep

Per-step scoring is **structurally blind** to a pattern applied consistently but wrongly: it
passes every individual review. On this project a systematic spacing error survived five commits
and every score, and was only found afterwards. This phase exists for that.

Run it in two directions, internal first.

### Internal — does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric. One question: is this internally consistent?

- Every recipe the same shape — same `parts` convention, same registration, same naming
- Every component the same structure — export, props type, story, test
- Every token used the same way for the same purpose
- The same value not typed twice in two places

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible.

### External — does that shared shape conform?

Only once you know what the feature's own pattern *is*:

- **The exemplar PR** — does the feature match what it established? Where the exemplar is itself
  inconsistent, say which variant this work followed and whether that was the better choice. Do
  not report a divergence from an unstable pattern as a defect.
- **`.claude/rules/*`** — do the rules hold across the whole feature, not just per file?
- **Figma, end to end** — the rendered feature against the named nodes, every variant and state.
  Remember the node-type discriminator and never cross-compare the two Figma files.

Use `zm-tester` for this, fanning out across the feature rather than one step. Every finding
carries **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — at this scope, UNIFORM is what you are hunting.

---

## Phase 3 — if the audit fails

**Hand back to `zimmerMANNBuild`. Do not fix it here.**

The auditor becoming the author is exactly the independence that makes this phase worth running,
and Build has a Scorer and a rework cap that this skill does not.

Report the defect with its evidence, return the work, and **re-audit when it comes back.** A
re-audit is a fresh pass, not a check that the named item changed.

---

## Phase 4 — the PR

Write the body yourself. Do not call `/pr-checklist` — its output is the team's format, and this
one is yours.

**The body describes the diff that actually shipped, not the plan.** If the two differ, the diff
wins and the difference is worth a line.

Include: what changed and why · the tier of every touched file, with any Tier 2 approver named ·
what was tested and the real numbers · anything deliberately deferred, with the owning ticket ·
anything left unverified.

**Never in a PR title, body, commit message or code comment:**
- Claude attribution of any kind — no `Co-Authored-By`, no mention
- CodeRabbit mentions
- A citation of any local-only doc. `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are Marcel's
  personal files. Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite that.
- Draft or pending disclaimers

Match the house standard by reading Marcel's own previously authored PRs on this repo, not by
inferring a format.

---

## Phase 5 — write it down, then present

**First write `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md`:**

```
# PostBuild — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Head: <sha>   Audited: <date>

## Audit — findings.md
| # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence |
<one row per row of findings.md. For every 🟡 CLARIFY: did the assumption hold?>

## Audit — plan.md
| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
<plus: files in the diff that were not in the manifest>

## Sweep — internal consistency
<does the feature agree with itself — recipes, structure, token use>

## Sweep — external conformance
<exemplar PR · .claude/rules/* · Figma end to end>

## UNIFORM findings
<the ones a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## PR body as written
<the exact text>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>
```

**Then append a block per review round**, as the loop runs:

```
## Round <n> — <date>
Findings received: <n> (CodeRabbit <n>, reviewer <n>)
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
<VALID / INVALID / OUT OF SCOPE / DEFER, with the evidence for each decline>
```

This file is read by **`zimmerMANNBuild rework`** — so it knows what was already declined and why,
rather than re-litigating it — and by **`zimmerMANNDevImprover`**. Write it even when the audit is
clean; a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Then present

Give him, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register:

1. The diff summary — files, tiers, commits
2. The audit result — every gate item and plan step, with anything that failed
3. The sweep result — **UNIFORM findings first**, they are the point of this skill
4. The proposed PR title and body
5. What could not be verified

Then **stop.**

**On his go: push and open the PR.** Not before. Push is the first irreversible, outward-facing
step in the chain, and it is his to authorise.

---

## Phase 6 — the review loop

When CodeRabbit or a reviewer requests changes:

1. **Hand the findings to `zimmerMANNBuild rework`.** It verifies each finding is real before
   anything is touched — CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo — then fixes and
   commits the valid ones.

2. **Draft a reply for every finding when it comes back.** Every thread gets a written answer:
   - **Fixed** — what changed, and the commit
   - **Declined** — the specific quotable repo rule, doc, or empirical result that makes it wrong.
     Not an opinion.
   - **Deferred** — the owning ticket or the person who decides

   **A fix commit with no in-thread reply does not count.** A prior PR here carried 18 threads with
   zero human replies; the process was being followed on the PR before it and was dropped entirely.

3. **Show him the full batch, then post on his go.** One approval covers the set.

4. Repeat until approved. If CodeRabbit raises the same objection a third time, stop re-running it
   and answer the threads instead — it has nothing to learn from unanswered comments.

**Before final hand-off, re-run the manifest check — not just once, at the end.** Phase 2's
manifest-versus-diff audit is a snapshot, not a standing guarantee. Any fix round in this phase
(a CodeRabbit rework, a reviewer's requested change, or a gap Marcel spots and Build fixes
directly) can add a file outside the original manifest — including a legitimate, individually-
authorized Tier 1/2 exception. If it does, that file belongs in the plan's manifest and in
postbuild.md's own audit paragraph, not left for the audit to silently go stale. Before presenting
the final state for merge, confirm the manifest audit's claim still matches `git diff
<base>..HEAD --numstat` exactly — if it doesn't, append a dated correction (same pattern as
plan.md's own "Open questions" section) rather than leaving the original claim uncorrected.

---

## The owner rule — everywhere outward-facing

The audit report, the PR body, and every reply.

Every finding names **who resolves it**: Marcel, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA. A blocker owned by the
designer and one owned by Marcel need different actions.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question to them — never a directive.**
"Should this route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before anything posts, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as
hiding behind their authority.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** Every fix goes back to Build. This skill audits, writes, and posts.
- **Never push or post without an explicit go.** Both are outward-facing and irreversible in
  practice.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never re-litigate a settled decision.** If the plan decided it and the build honoured it, it
  is not a finding — report a *mechanical consequence* of a decision, never the decision.
- **Say what you could not verify.** An audit that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

content.text:
Root cause confirmed via the real SDK type defs (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`), not guesswork — two real bugs in the search call:

1. **`htype` isn't a top-level parameter at all** — the real type only has `refine?: string`; `htype=master` is a *value* that belongs inside `refine`, the same way the existing base `HomepageContent` code already does it. My `htype: 'master'` was a bogus key that silently type-checked (the SDK's params type is permissive) but did nothing at runtime — so the search was never actually scoped to master-level hits.
2. **`allImages` was never passed.** Per the SDK's own doc comment: *"If no flag is passed, the `imageGroups` property is omitted from the response"* — regardless of `expand` including `'images'`. That's the direct, documented cause of `imageGroups: undefined`, not the `viewType` filter I originally suspected.

Fixing both now.

content.text:
Good catch — checked, and the cards themselves aren't actually built wrong. `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` documents this explicitly:

> "The Large variant (288×432) and the Small/mobile variant (179×268) both resolve to the same ~2:3 ratio — expressed here as a ratio, not either variant's sampled pixel dimensions, per the card's **'fluid, not a fixed px width' contract**."

So `ZimmProductCard`'s image is deliberately `width: 100%` + `aspect-ratio: 2/3`, not a fixed pixel size — it's meant to fill whatever column width it's given. The bug is on my side: when I switched to `SimpleGrid` with a fixed 4-column count, on a real wide desktop viewport each column ends up much wider than Figma's reference 288px, and the aspect-ratio-locked image scales right up with it — that's what's making the whole card look oversized.

Fix: cap each card at 288px (Figma's own confirmed desktop reference width, cited in that same file's docblock) and center it within its grid column, so narrower breakpoints are unaffected but wide desktop columns stop stretching the card past spec.

Each section has an on-page note explaining anything that isn't a separate buildable card — the three mobile-viewport-gated behaviors (tell you which existing card to resize the browser against instead of duplicating it), the real `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` reveal (provable on any interactive card here, which Storybook can't do), and the Recently Viewed / Wishlist framing.

**What I did *not* add, and why** (all confirmed via the research pass, documented in the file's own updated docblock):
- **Hero variant** — orphaned Figma node, no owning ticket, no 4th `variation` value exists in the component.
- **Tablet-specific design** — no such Figma variant exists.
- **Recently Viewed *carousel*** (SFCC-83) — a different surface from the Full History grid shown here; genuinely has no code path today.
- **Three Wishlist CRM-backed states** (a distinct "What's Now" price type, a region-unavailable state, a destructive add-to-bag treatment) — PRD-confirmed but never actually built into the shipped component, so there's nothing real to demo.
- **VIC/customer-group price precedence** — explicitly deferred to SFCC-778.

One thing worth your attention, not mine to resolve here: the Wishlist section's note flags that the shipped hover-revealed size-chip picker matches PLP/Figma, but the literal Jira AC text for Wishlist only calls out image-swap + arrows on hover. That's an already-accepted design-over-AC-text call from earlier in this build, not something introduced by this demo — surfacing it since you wanted the ACs directly checkable.

Both clean. Summary of the aesthetic pass:

- **Title-cased everything**: category headings (`Core Component`, `PLP`, `Home`, `Wishlist`, `Recently Viewed (Full History)`) and every card label (`Default`, `Out of Stock`, `One Size`, `Single Image`, `Hover-Swap Pair`, `Multiple Images`, `Sale Price`, `Loading Price`, `Recently Viewed 1–4`).
- **Trimmed the verbose parenthetical labels** (e.g. `Default (badge/hover-swap suppressed)` → just `Default`) — that detail is already carried by each section's descriptive note, so the card labels now read cleanly as short state names instead of run-on captions.
- **Restyled the per-card labels** from plain body text to a small uppercase tag (`textStyle="label"`, muted colour) — matches the `N ITEMS` treatment already in the header, and reads as a meta-label rather than blending into the real product-card content beneath it.
- **Added a divider** between the five sections (`--zimm-border-width-default` / `--zimm-color-border-default`, both real registered tokens) so the now-larger page reads as distinct, separable groups rather than one long uninterrupted scroll.

Refresh and take a look.

#!/bin/bash
# commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
#
# Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
#          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

commit_msg=$(cat "$1")

# Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
  exit 0
fi

# Conventional commits pattern
# type(optional-scope): description
# upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'

if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
  echo ""
  echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
  echo ""
  echo "  Types:"
  echo "    feat           new feature"
  echo "    fix            bug fix"
  echo "    docs           documentation only"
  echo "    style          formatting, no logic change"
  echo "    refactor       neither fix nor feat"
  echo "    perf           performance improvement"
  echo "    test           adding or updating tests"
  echo "    build          build system or dependency changes"
  echo "    ci             CI/CD configuration"
  echo "    chore          maintenance tasks"
  echo "    upstream-sync  upstream Salesforce PWA Kit sync"
  echo ""
  echo "  Scope examples (optional but encouraged):"
  echo "    product-tile  checkout  auth  header  search"
  echo "    global-e  adyen  contentful  searchspring"
  echo "    pwa-kit-runtime  commerce-sdk-react"
  echo ""
  echo "  Examples:"

  echo "    fix(checkout): resolve shipping method not persisting on refresh"
  echo "    upstream-sync(pwa-kit-runtime): apply v3.18.0 SSR cache fix"
  echo "    chore(deps): update @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react to 5.3.0"
  echo "    test(use-current-basket): add guest basket merge coverage"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

exit 0

If the arrows/other hover-revealed content are set to `display: none` by default and only flipped to `display: flex`/`block` via `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` on an ANCESTOR, consider: (a) can a screen reader (VoiceOver) still "see"/announce elements that are `display:none` in the accessibility tree at all — normally no, they're removed entirely; so if VoiceOver users can't reach revealed content via swipe/rotor because it's `display:none` until an ancestor gets `:focus-visible`, and VoiceOver's own focus/interaction model doesn't reliably trigger `:focus-visible` the same way a physical Tab key-press does, that's a real candidate root cause — investigate whether this exact mismatch is what's happening; (b) whether keyboard Tab order reaches the arrows/other revealed controls in a broken order, skips them, or effectively traps focus; (c) whether the "stuck open" bug that `:has(:focus-visible)` was meant to fix might have overcorrected by making the reveal LESS accessible via keyboard than before (e.g. requiring focus to remain within a specific descendant that keyboard nav doesn't naturally land on).

Report back: the exact commit SHAs and diffs found, the exact current CSS/DOM mechanism (file + line numbers), and your best-supported theory (or theories, ranked) for the specific keyboard-nav and screen-reader breakage the developer is describing. Do not propose a fix yet — this is investigation only, feeding into a plan. Be thorough and cite exact file:line locations for everything you assert.

input.prompt:
We're on git branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component in this repo (a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront). The developer reports: "the multiple images state on mobile doesn't work on swipe — the slide indicator is there, but the swipe/gesture isn't focusing on swiping through the images." I need you to find the exact mechanism so we can plan a fix.

Background already known (don't re-derive from scratch, verify and go deeper):
- The component is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`, composed inside `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`.
- The gallery is native CSS scroll-snap: a `scrollContainer` div (`overflowX: 'auto'`, `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`, `WebkitOverflowScrolling: 'touch'`, scrollbar hidden) containing `slide` children (`flex: '0 0 100%'`, `scrollSnapAlign: 'start'`).
- The touch-only slide indicator (`ZimmSlideIndicator`, rendered when `totalSlides > 1`) is meant to track the ACTIVE slide as the user swipes — it listens for a native `scrollend` event on the scroll container and computes the nearest slide from `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth` (see the `useEffect` with `handleScrollEnd` in `index.tsx`).
- Desktop hover-only prev/next arrow buttons exist in the same component; a separate always-on keyboard handler (`onKeyDown` on the scroll container, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight) also calls `goToRelativeSlide`, which calls `scrollTo({left, behavior:'smooth'})` on the container.
- The developer's report is specific: the indicator dot UI is visibly present (so `totalSlides > 1` is true and images did load), but the actual touch swipe gesture doesn't scroll/page through the images at all on a real mobile device.

What to actually investigate and report:

<result>## Investigation Findings — Mobile Swipe Not Paging the Gallery

I read both components (and their `.css.ts` files) in full, plus `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, `zimmSlideIndicator`, `zimmProductCardContent`, `globalStyles.ts`, git history, both test files, e2e coverage, and `playwright.config.js`. Findings below map to your 7 numbered checks, then a ranked-theory synthesis.

### 1–2. The current mechanism (confirmed, nothing new vs. your brief)

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`:
- `scrollContainerRef` attached at line 229, on the div styled by `styles.scrollContainer` (line 230).
- Only handler on that div is `onKeyDown={handleScrollContainerKeyDown}` (line 235) — ArrowLeft/ArrowRight only (lines 191–195). No `onTouchStart`/`onPointerDown`/`onClick` anywhere on the container or its ancestors.
- `scrollend` listener (lines 203–215) only *reads* `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth` to update the indicator — never calls `preventDefault`, never blocks anything.
- `badge`/`close`/`carousel`/`indicatorWrapper` (lines 274–317) are DOM **siblings** of `scrollContainer`, not children of it.

`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`:
- `scrollContainer` (lines 65–84): `display:flex, width:'100%', overflowX:'auto', scrollSnapType:'x mandatory', WebkitOverflowScrolling:'touch', scrollbarWidth:'none'` + `_focusVisible`. **No `position`, no `height`, no `touchAction` key at all.**
- `slide` (lines 86–97): `position:'relative', flex:'0 0 100%', width:'100%', aspectRatio:'2 / 3', scrollSnapAlign:'start', overflow:'hidden'`. No `transform`/`will-change`.
- `carousel` (lines 172–195): `position:'absolute', transform:'translateY(-50%)', display:'none'` (unconditional at this file's level), `pointerEvents:'none'` (wrapper, line 194) / `'auto'` (arrowButton, line 207). Reveal now lives *only* in the organism recipe's `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` — which never matches a touchscreen, so on a real phone this part is never rendered/painted at all (irrelevant to the bug on mobile).
- `indicatorWrapper` (lines 217–226): `position:absolute, left:0, right:0, bottom:0`, no explicit height — sized to `ZimmSlideIndicator`'s own 1px hairline (`zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:32`, `height: var(--zimm-scale-025)`). Too small to be a plausible invisible hit-area over the image. Ruled out.

**`touch-action`**: repo-wide `grep -rniE "touch-action|touchAction"` across every `.ts/.tsx/.scss/.css` (excluding node_modules) returns **zero hits**. It is not set anywhere — not in this component family, not in `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` (read in full — only typography/grid/form/focus utility classes, nothing touch-related), not in any Chakra recipe. This rules out the classic "`touch-action: pan-y`/`none` on an ancestor" cause entirely.

### 3. Transform/stacking-context and container sizing

- No `transform`/`will-change` on `scrollContainer` or `slide` — only `carousel` (a sibling, `display:none` on touch) has `transform`, and it doesn't nest inside `scrollContainer`, so it can't break scroll-snap there.
- `scrollContainer` has no explicit height/width beyond `width:'100%'`; height is derived from `slide`'s `aspectRatio` via flex layout — nothing structurally suspicious, and `aspect-ratio` is within this project's stated browserslist (iOS ≥ 17, Android ≥ 14, per `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own docblock). I found no code-level evidence of a 0-width-collapse bug; this would need a live/Playwright render to fully exclude, but nothing points at it.

### 4. The actual finding: whole-card stretched-link overlay sits on top of the gallery, untested for this exact surface

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts:219-223`:
```
[`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] a::after`]: {
  content: '""',
  position: 'absolute',
  inset: 0,
},
```
This targets the real `<a>` (`ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink)`, defined `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:39`, rendered at line 210 inside `data-card-slot="content"` at line 208). I verified independently (not just trusting the docblock) that neither `ZimmProductCardContent`'s `root`, `nameRow`, nor `nameLink` sets `position` anywhere — `grep -n position zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` returns **zero matches**. So the `position:absolute; inset:0` containing block for this `::after` resolves to the nearest ancestor that *does* set `position`, which is the **organism root** (`zimmProductCard.css.ts:213`, `position:'relative'`), not `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own box. The file's own docblock (lines 59–61) confirms this explicitly: *"`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root` IS `position: relative`, but Media is a sibling of Content under this organism's root, never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain."* Net effect: **the invisible overlay is sized to the entire card — image area and text area both** — not just the name row.

Critically, this overlay carries **no `z-index`, deliberately** (docblock lines 194–199; proven by the recipe's own test, `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx:507-514`, which asserts `hasOwnProperty(after,'zIndex') === false`). The recipe then explicitly lifts exactly three things above it, and only three, `zimmProductCard.css.ts:240-253`:
```
[`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.close}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },          // line 240-242
[`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },       // line 247-249
[`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {              // line 250-253
  position: 'relative', zIndex: 1,
},
```
The docblock's own reasoning for why (lines 62–64): *"a z-index higher than the overlay's own (left unset), **or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first**."* This is the codebase itself stating, in writing, that anything not on this list gets its clicks intercepted by the overlay.

There is **no equivalent lift for `[data-card-slot="media"]`, `scrollContainer`, or `slide`** — confirmed via `grep -n "CARD_SLOT.media"` on `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: zero matches. `scrollContainer` doesn't even carry a `data-card-slot` attribute (only Media's outermost `root` does, `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:227`). `scrollContainer` itself is `position:static` (no `position` key at all, confirmed above), and `slide` is `position:relative` with `z-index:auto` — un-lifted.

Because `ZimmProductCardMedia` renders **before** `ZimmProductCardContent` in the organism (`zimmProductCard/index.tsx:441-450` then `451-470`), and neither Media's root nor the organism's own root establishes a real stacking context (`position:relative` with `z-index:auto` doesn't create one per CSS2.1 — only a set z-index, transform, opacity<1, filter, or isolation would), the `<a>::after` (positioned, z-index:auto) and `scrollContainer`/`slide` end up compared in the same ancestor stacking context, where a positioned element always paints above non-positioned in-flow content, and among same-level positioned/auto elements the later one in DOM order (Content) wins. Either way the result is the same: **the overlay paints, and therefore hit-tests, on top of the whole image/gallery region.**

This is exactly the same bug *class* this codebase has already caught and fixed once — for the desktop arrow buttons (Fix 3, `zimmProductCard.css.ts` docblock lines 84–101, and `index.test.tsx:525-539` / `843-866`): a `transform`-induced stacking context trapped the arrows' own z-index so real clicks landed on the overlay "despite passing every jsdom test," only caught by "the manual real-browser check performed after the round-2 Scorer PASS." That audit pass evidently covered `close`/`carousel`/content buttons (click targets) but was never extended to the touch/swipe gesture on the image itself.

The test suite's own **"KNOWN LIMITATION"** docblock (`zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx:312-328`) states this gap explicitly and by name:
> *"jsdom performs no real layout, paint, or hit-testing (no CSS cascade resolution, no stacking-context/z-index comparison, no geometry at all)... going from 'the right CSS values exist' to 'a real browser click lands on the right element' is exactly the gap a real-browser (Playwright or manual) check is for."*

No test anywhere — jsdom or Playwright — exercises a click/touch/drag on `scrollContainer`/`slide`/the image itself to prove it isn't shadowed by this overlay. The one organism test that touches the carousel (`index.test.tsx:338`, "the carousel arrows fire independently of the name-link overlay") only clicks the arrow *buttons* (already lifted), never the image region.

Ancestor `onClick`/`onTouchStart`/`onPointerDown` with `preventDefault`: none found anywhere in the ancestor chain (`grep` across `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` and the organism `index.tsx` shows only ordinary `onClick` on the bag and notify-me buttons — unrelated to the swipe path).

`pointer-events`: only two occurrences in the whole `ui-kits` tree, both already read — `carousel` wrapper `pointerEvents:'none'` / `arrowButton` `'auto'` (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:194,207`) — both irrelevant on touch since `carousel` isn't rendered there.

### 5–7. Git history, tests, e2e — corroborating the theory

- Every commit touching these three files (`219d0a1` → `548b9d7`, ~11 commits) was inspected in full (subject + body). Every real-device-caught bug is described as found via **"manual real-browser check," "live-browser testing,"** or **"live Figma"** — one (`72ee2a9`) explicitly mentions a **Storybook**-specific fix ("Storybook placeholder-fill colour correction... dark fills were masking overlays in Storybook"). **None of the ~11 commits mention "touch," "swipe," "mobile device," or a Playwright/mobile run.** The verification method that did catch stacking bugs (Fix 1: close button knocked out of position; Fix 3: carousel arrows unclickable) was demonstrably desktop-mouse-click testing, not touch-drag testing.
- `ZimmProductCard` is **not yet consumed by any page/grid** — `grep` for consumers outside its own folder only finds `zimmProductCardShared.ts` and the theme recipe registry (`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:33-35,70-72`). The only place it currently renders anywhere is its own `index.stories.tsx` and its Vitest suite. So any "real mobile device" check the developer did was necessarily against **Storybook's own iframe render of this isolated organism** — which doesn't add or remove any ancestor overlay (no page-level grid wrapper exists yet to introduce a *different* bug), so it reproduces the exact same stretched-link-over-gallery DOM/CSS. This actually reinforces the theory rather than complicating it: the bug is fully self-contained inside these two components today.
- `e2e/tests/zimm/` contains only `homepage/SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js`, `homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js`, and `homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js` — **nothing referencing `zimmProductCard`/`zimmProductCardMedia` at all.**
- `playwright.config.js:64-68` **does** define a `mobile-chrome` project (`devices['Pixel 5']`) and the repo already has a mobile-spec-folder precedent (`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/`) — so the infrastructure to catch this with a real touch-emulated Playwright run exists, it has simply never been pointed at this component. Nothing in the codebase uses `page.touchscreen` or any swipe/drag simulation for this gallery.
- `zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` only exercises: `scrollTo` call shape via click on arrow buttons (lines 146–175), the `scrollend`→indicator wiring via a synthetic `Event('scrollend')` (lines 384–409), and keyboard ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (lines 411–429). **No touch/pointer/drag simulation exists anywhere in this file** — confirmed via `grep -n "touch\|swipe\|scroll"`.

### Ranked theories

1. **(Primary, strongly evidenced)** The organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay (`zimmProductCard.css.ts:219-223`, selector `[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`) is sized via `inset:0` to the entire card (image + text), carries no `pointer-events:none` and no `z-index`, and — unlike `close`/`carousel`/content buttons (`zimmProductCard.css.ts:240-253`) — has no corresponding lift for `media`/`scrollContainer`/`slide`. A touchstart landing on the image resolves to this overlay's owning `<a>` element (a sibling subtree of Media, never an ancestor of `scrollContainer`), so the browser's native scroll-gesture recognizer never engages `scrollContainer` at all — no scroll ever happens, `scrollend` never fires, and the indicator (purely state/prop-driven) sits there correctly rendered but never updates. This is the identical bug *class* already caught once for the desktop arrows (Fix 3) via manual real-browser testing that was never extended to the swipe surface — a gap the test suite's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock (`index.test.tsx:312-328`) names directly, and git history confirms no touch-specific verification (Playwright mobile or real device) was ever performed on this component.
2. **(Weak, unconfirmed, would need a live render to fully exclude)** Some real-device-only sizing quirk collapsing `scrollContainer`'s real scrollable width to ~0 despite working in Storybook/desktop — no supporting code evidence found (no explicit height, no transform, no touch-action interfering); ranked low-confidence.
3. **(Ruled out)** `touch-action` blocking horizontal panning — zero occurrences repo-wide.
4. **(Ruled out on real mobile)** Carousel `transform`-induced stacking context intercepting the swipe — `carousel` is `display:none` on any real touchscreen (gated behind `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` + organism `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`, which never matches a touch-only pointer), so it isn't even in the paint tree on mobile; only relevant as precedent for the same bug pattern.
5. **(Ruled out)** Ancestor `onClick`/`onTouchStart`/`onPointerDown` calling `preventDefault` — none exist in the ancestor chain besides the keyboard-only handler on the scroll container itself.

Files most relevant to cite in a fix plan: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts:219-223` (the overlay) and `:240-253` (the existing lift pattern to extend), `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:227-236` (root/scrollContainer, no `data-card-slot` on `scrollContainer` itself to target), and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx:312-328` (the limitation this bug fell through).</result>

content.text:
Swipe investigation is back with a strong, well-evidenced root cause. Still waiting on the hover/keyboard-nav investigation before I move to designing the fix plan, but here's what's confirmed on the swipe issue:

**Root cause**: The organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay (`zimmProductCard.css.ts:219-223`, the invisible `<a>::after` that makes the whole card clickable to the PDP) is sized to the *entire* card — image and text both — because `ZimmProductCardContent` itself never sets `position` anywhere, so the overlay's containing block resolves to the organism root, not just the name-link row. That overlay carries no `z-index`, and the recipe only explicitly lifts three things above it (`close`, `carousel`, and buttons inside `content`) — the image/gallery scroll container was never added to that lift list. Since neither the media root nor the organism root establishes a real stacking context on its own, the overlay ends up painting (and hit-testing) on top of the whole image area.

Net effect: a touch swipe on the image actually starts on the invisible overlay `<a>`, never reaches the actual scroll container, so the browser's native swipe-scroll gesture never engages — no scroll happens, the indicator (purely state-driven) just sits there unchanged. This is the exact same bug *class* already caught once before for the desktop arrow buttons, and caught only via manual real-browser testing — jsdom can't do real hit-testing, and this component has no Playwright coverage at all yet, so nothing would have caught it. `touch-action` isn't set anywhere in the codebase (ruled out as a separate cause).

Fix is a small, precedent-following addition: extend the existing z-index lift pattern to the media root's `data-card-slot="media"` selector, same as the three entries already there.

Holding on the plan until the keyboard/VoiceOver investigation lands.

This is a genuine regression introduced specifically by `983bddf`, not a pre-existing condition: the `:focus-within` mechanism it replaced (still described at `zimmProductCard.css.ts:105-109` as the design point 3 reasoning) has no input-modality dependency whatsoever — any focus, however it arrived, satisfied it. Trading it for `:has(:focus-visible)` fixed the "stuck open after a mouse click" bug at the cost of introducing exactly this AT-modality dependency.

Supporting evidence that this exact gap was never checked:
- Zero occurrences of "VoiceOver," "screen reader," or "aria-live" anywhere in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/` or `.../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/` (confirmed by grep across both directories).

Before `72ee2a9`, the arrows were unconditionally `display: 'flex'` on any hover-capable device (the old `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` sub-block on `carousel` in `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`, removed by that commit) — so they were always a stable, predictable tab stop, independent of any prior interaction. But Shift+Tab entry into the card from *after* it (returning from a later element, e.g. the next card in a grid) lands on whatever the last unconditionally-visible tabbable element is at that moment — traced through the verified DOM order above, that's the **bag button** (`zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:214-232`), since price is non-interactive and size-chips/arrows/notify-me are all still `display: none`. input.prompt:
Context: repo is a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann), branch `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`. A thorough investigation (already done, don't re-run it — verify specifics by reading the cited files directly) found the following. I need you to design a concrete, technically sound fix — this is genuinely non-obvious, not a rubber-stamp.

## The mechanism (verified, current HEAD `8959718`)

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s `root` part has a single `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block (`HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)'`, defined in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmProductCardShared.ts`) gating FIVE separate hover-reveals, each via a paired `&:hover ...` / `&:has(:focus-visible) ...` selector (lines ~284-385):
1. Home price reveal
2. PLP/Wishlist price hide (a swap, not additive)
3. PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal
4. Notify-me reveal
5. Carousel arrow reveal (`[data-card-slot="carousel"]`, its own base `display:none` lives in the composed molecule `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`)

History (3 commits, all on this branch, verified via git log/show):
- `72ee2a9` moved the carousel-arrow reveal from a device-CAPABILITY check (always visible on any hover-capable device) to this real interaction-gated reveal.
- `983bddf` replaced `:focus-within` with `:has(:focus-visible)` at all five sites, because `:focus-within` doesn't clear on `mouseleave` once a mouse click gives a button real DOM focus — arrows/etc. stayed stuck visible after mouse-out until a click landed entirely outside the card. This is a real, confirmed, desirable fix for that specific "stuck open after mouse click" bug — do NOT propose simply reverting it wholesale, that reintroduces a real bug.
- `8959718` (current HEAD) is test-only, unrelated to the actual mechanism.

The organism's own component (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`, ~line 348-350) states its explicit design principle: both molecules always render in full; CSS ALONE decides what is visible — no JS-tracked reveal state today. Treat this as the status quo to respect if a fix can reasonably do so, but you may propose deviating from it if that's genuinely the right call — just say so explicitly and why, don't silently break it.

## Why this is now a real accessibility regression (verified)

- `:focus-visible` (and `:has(:focus-visible)`) is a browser HEURISTIC for "does this focus event look keyboard-like" — not a strict, guaranteed-consistent check. VoiceOver's own navigation model (VO+Arrow, rotor navigation, swipe) moves real DOM focus onto elements without necessarily being treated as "keyboard modality" by the browser engine, and this varies by engine/OS version — a real, documented category of mismatch.
- `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is TRUE on any Mac laptop with a trackpad — so this is NOT a touch-only concern. A VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook hardware is exactly the population this gate applies to.
- If VoiceOver-driven focus doesn't satisfy `:focus-visible`, all five reveals stay `display:none` for that entire session, for that user, no matter how they navigate — `display:none` unconditionally removes an element from the accessibility tree (not "hard to reach," "doesn't exist for AT at all").
- Separately (a secondary, lower-severity but also real and verified issue): because these controls only exist as Tab stops WHILE a hover/focus-visible condition is currently true, the set of Tab stops in the card changes based on interaction history, not just DOM structure. Forward-Tab into the card works fine (landing on the always-present scroll-container region triggers the reveal before the user would reach the arrows). But Shift+Tab entry into the card from something AFTER it (e.g. the next card in a grid, once one exists) lands on the last unconditionally-visible tabbable element (the bag button) — the user has already tabbed past the (at that instant nonexistent) arrows/size-chip-radio/notify-me and must reverse direction to reach them. Real, but recoverable — not a hard trap.
- No CSS media feature exists to detect "a screen reader is active" (deliberately, for privacy reasons) — so a pure-CSS "detect AT and do something different" approach is not available.
- Existing test coverage would NOT catch a fix regressing this again: there are zero Storybook `play` functions in this component family (every relevant story's own docblock says Storybook can't force a `hover:hover` media context), and the Vitest suite's own "Fix 2" describe block (organism `index.test.tsx`, from ~line 899) asserts against a hand-built stand-in div substituting for the real card root, not `getComputedStyle` on the real composed tree post-focus (the file's own comments explain jsdom can't dynamically re-resolve pseudo-class-gated styles that way).

## What I need from you

Design a concrete fix. Specifically:

1. Read `zimmProductCard.css.ts` in full (all 5 reveal sites + docblock points 3, 6, and the "Fix H" note explaining the `:focus-within`→`:has(:focus-visible)` change) and `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel`/`arrowButton` parts, plus `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`'s `scrollContainer` JSX and its keyboard handler, to ground your design in the real current code, not just this summary.
2. Propose 1-2 concrete technical approaches that resolve BOTH the AT-inaccessibility (Theory 1) and the stateful-tab-order issue (Theory 2) without reintroducing the mouse "stuck open" bug `983bddf` fixed. Consider explicitly: is there a way to keep these controls PRESENT in the accessibility tree and Tab order at all times (not `display:none` by default), visually hiding them via a proper "visually-hidden but AT/keyboard-operable" technique (the standard sr-only/clip pattern) instead, and only using `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` to toggle the VISUAL treatment — while making sure this doesn't reintroduce the stuck-open bug for sighted mouse users, and doesn't put sighted keyboard users through a confusing "landed on an invisible control" experience. Also consider whether decoupling this from pure CSS (a minimal, targeted JS focus/hover-state approach only for the parts that need it) is actually simpler/more correct than trying to force a CSS-only solution — and if so, be concrete about exactly what state and event listeners, and exactly how it avoids re-introducing the stuck-open bug.
3. For each approach: what changes (file + what kind of change, not full code), what it fixes, what tradeoff or residual risk it carries, and how it could actually be verified (a Storybook play function can't force real hover, so what real check would prove this works — real Playwright with a forced-modality focus, real manual VoiceOver testing, or something else).
4. Recommend ONE approach as the primary path, with the other(s) as an appendix/alternative, not multiple parallel plans.

Do not write any code. Do not modify any files. This is a design/planning task — return your analysis and recommendation as text.
