message.content: ELI5

content.text:
Sure — simple version:

**Swipe fix:** We moved the photo "on top" of an invisible full-card link so your finger could actually reach it to swipe. But that also means a plain click on the photo now has to be handled by our own new code instead of that invisible link. Our new code does the basic "click → go to product page" part, but it forgot to check for the standard tricks — Cmd/Ctrl-click to open in a new tab, middle-click, etc. Those just silently stop working now. Swiping itself is still fine — this is only about clicking.

**Screen-reader fix:** Five things (price, size picker, notify-me, arrows) only show up on hover/focus. They used to hide themselves in a way that also made them invisible to screen readers *and* Tab key navigation. We fixed that for all five, so a desktop screen-reader/keyboard user can now find them properly.

The catch: two of those five (size picker + arrows) are *also* supposed to be permanently hidden on phones/tablets, since there's no "hover" there at all — that part was already correct and untouched. But our fix for the desktop problem accidentally made them "tabbable-but-invisible forever" on touch devices too, for anyone using an external keyboard with a tablet. It's a small trap: you can Tab onto something you can never see or use. CodeRabbit caught this for the size picker; I checked the same pattern and found the arrows have it too, un-flagged.

The other three things we fixed (price both ways, notify-me) don't have this problem — they don't need a hover to become visible on touch, so there's no trap there.

**Slide-indicator lag fix:** Not related to either finding at all — completely separate, still solid.

content.text:
Committed at `79384ad`. Now drafting the CodeRabbit replies — natural, technical tone, referencing the actual fix.

**Reply to Finding #1 (`handleMediaClick` modifier-click handling, `index.tsx:469-473`):**

> Good catch, verified and fixed in `79384ad`. `handleMediaClick` now bails out on `event.metaKey`/`ctrlKey`/`shiftKey`/`altKey` or a non-primary button, so a modifier-click or middle-click no longer forces an in-tab `history.push` — it falls through and does nothing instead, same as it would if the click had landed outside the card. That's not quite full parity with a real `<a>` (it doesn't open a new tab the way native anchor semantics would), but it's the right tradeoff here: not silently overriding an explicit "open elsewhere" signal matters more than replicating the exact browser chrome behavior, and going further (e.g. `window.open`) felt like scope creep for what this handler actually needs to guarantee. Added `test.each`-based coverage for all five cases (Cmd, Ctrl, Shift, Alt, non-primary button) so this can't silently regress again.

**Reply to Finding #2 (touch-pointer size-selector state, `zimmProductCard.css.ts:400-411`):**

> Confirmed and fixed in `79384ad` — and it turned out to be a slightly bigger fix than just this one spot. You're right that the unconditional `clip-path` here left the size-selector permanently tabbable-but-invisible on touch, since `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` never matches there and there's no other reveal path. # SFCC-236: fix two live-testing regressions in ZimmProductCard

## Context

While testing PR #85 (`feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`) live, Marcel found two
real bugs in the shared `ZimmProductCard` family:

**(a) A recent hover-reveal fix broke keyboard nav and VoiceOver.** The most recent fix on this
branch (`983bddf`) replaced `:focus-within` with `:has(:focus-visible)` across five hover-reveal
sites, specifically to stop the carousel arrows (and everything else gated the same way) from
staying visible after a mouse click even once the mouse moved away — a real, correctly-diagnosed
bug, and that part of the fix is not being reverted. The regression is elsewhere: every one of
those five reveals uses `display: 'none'` as its "hidden" state, gated behind an *interaction*
heuristic (`:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`). `display: none` unconditionally strips an element
from the accessibility tree — it answers "is this painted," not "does this exist for assistive
tech," and this recipe has been using it to answer both questions at once. `:focus-visible` is
itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven
focus (VO+Arrow, rotor, swipe) is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every engine — a real, documented
mismatch, and *not* a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac
trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook hardware is exactly the population this gate
applies to. If that heuristic never matches for a given user, all five reveals (carousel arrows,
Home's price reveal, PLP/Wishlist's price↔size-selector swap, notify-me) stay invisible to them
for the entire session, no matter how they navigate. A secondary, lower-severity effect confirmed
alongside it: because these controls only exist as Tab stops *while* the interaction condition is
currently true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something after it lands on the last
unconditionally-visible stop (the bag button) — the user has already tabbed past controls that,
at that instant, didn't exist yet, and must reverse direction to reach them. (Forward-Tab is fine:
landing on the always-present scroll container triggers the reveal before reaching the arrows.)

**(b) Multi-image cards don't respond to touch swipe on mobile.** The slide indicator renders
correctly (so the image data and gallery logic are fine), but swiping the image doesn't page
through it at all. Root cause: the organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay
(`[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`, `position: absolute; inset: 0`) resolves its containing
block to the organism root — because `ZimmProductCardContent` never sets `position` anywhere —
so it's sized to the *entire* card, image included, not just the name-link row. That overlay
carries no `z-index`, and the recipe already lifts exactly three things above it (`close`,
`carousel`, buttons inside `content`) — the media/gallery scroll region was never added to that
list. A touch swipe on the image actually starts on the invisible overlay `<a>`, so the browser's
native swipe-scroll gesture never engages the real scroll container at all.

Both root causes were confirmed via direct investigation of this exact code (file/line citations
below) before any fix was designed, and both fixes reuse patterns already shipped elsewhere in
this same codebase rather than inventing anything new — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s already-tested
off-page-swatch technique for (a), and this recipe's own existing z-index-lift pattern for (b).

## Fix (b) — swipe blocked by the stretched-link overlay

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`
(styling), plus a small behavioral addition in `.../organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` and/or
`.../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` (exact home for the new handler decided at
implementation time — see the click-passthrough note below).

- Add a fourth lift entry alongside the existing three (currently lines 240-253):
  ```
  [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },
  ```
  `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position: 'relative'` (its own recipe), so only
  `zIndex` is needed here — identical in shape to the existing `close`/`carousel` entries.
- Extend docblock point 2 (the "lifting every interactive control" explanation, ~lines 62-101)
  with a new dated fix note, continuing this file's own Fix 1/Fix 3/Fix H lettered convention,
  explaining the media/gallery region needed the same lift the click targets already got, and
  that this was missed because clicking `close`/`carousel`/content-buttons was checked live but
  swiping the image itself never was.
- Extend `index.test.tsx`'s existing z-index-lift describe block (or add a sibling one) to assert
  the new entry's object shape, matching that file's own established idiom for these proofs.

**Click-passthrough — required, not optional (caught by Marcel during plan review).** Lifting the
media area above the overlay fixes the swipe, but it also means a plain tap/click on the image
would stop navigating to the PDP: today, that tap works *because* it hits the invisible overlay
link underneath; once media sits on top, it doesn't reach that link anymore, and the image itself
has no click handler of its own. Needed addition:
- Give the media root its own `onClick` that navigates to the same product URL the overlay already
  points to (the organism already receives `href` as part of its own base props, so this needs no
  new prop plumbing from outside — just forwarding it to wherever the new handler lives). No custom
  drag-detection logic is needed for this to behave correctly: browsers natively suppress the
  synthetic `click` event after a real drag/scroll on the same element, so a swipe won't trigger
  navigation, while a plain tap (no movement) still fires the click exactly as it does today.
- **Guard against the three things already inside media that must keep their own click behavior**
  (the two arrow buttons — page the gallery — and the remove/`close` button — removes from
  wishlist): the new handler must check whether the click's target is a `<button>` (or has one as
  an ancestor within media) and, if so, do nothing — rather than modifying each of those three
  existing button handlers individually. Confirm the exact current navigation mechanism `nameLink`
  uses (it's `ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink)` in `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx`) and reuse
  the same one for consistency, rather than introducing a second navigation method into this
  component family.

**Verification:** jsdom cannot prove this (no stacking-context resolution — this file's own
"KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock already says so). Needs a real touch check: Playwright's
`mobile-chrome` project with a real drag/swipe gesture on the image (confirming it pages and does
NOT navigate), a real tap with no movement (confirming it DOES navigate), and a real click on each
of the arrow buttons and the remove button (confirming neither now also navigates) — or the
equivalent manual check on Marcel's own device.

## Fix (a) — hover-reveal content invisible to VoiceOver / skipped on Shift+Tab

**Files:** `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (all 5 reveal sites) and
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
(carousel's own base state)

**Recommended fix** — keep every one of the five reveal targets permanently present in the DOM,
focusable, and in the accessibility tree at all times. Stop using `display` to express "hidden";
use the exact technique `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already ships for its own off-page swatches
(confirmed real, `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:215`:
`{ position: 'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)' }`):

- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` instead of
  `display: 'none'` — out of flow (no layout gap, same as today), paints nothing, but stays in
  the DOM/tab order/accessibility tree.
- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte
  unchanged — this is the entire point: the trigger logic from `983bddf` is not being touched):
  `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` instead of `display: 'block'/'flex'`.
- Applies at all 5 sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: Home price reveal (~293-297, 323-325),
  PLP/Wishlist price hide (~330-332, 338-340), PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal (~344-346,
  348-350), notify-me reveal (~359-362, 364-366), carousel arrow reveal (~379-384).
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part: its own unconditional base `display: 'none'`
  becomes the same clip-path equivalent (already `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally, so only
  the hidden-state property changes).
- **Carousel-specific addition:** the wrapper deliberately sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` with each
  `arrowButton` individually re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so clicks in the empty centre
  pass through to the image). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, add an explicit
  belt-and-braces rule in the organism recipe — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets
  `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `'auto'` only in the two revealed selectors — rather than
  relying on clip-path's hit-testing suppression alone. (Price/size-selector/notify-me need no
  equivalent — none of them sets `pointerEvents` at all today.)

**Why this is the recommended path, not one of several open options** (a JS-tracked hover/focus
state was considered and rejected): there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more
than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated." A hand-rolled heuristic (e.g.
flagging `focusin` as non-keyboard when preceded by `pointerdown`) has exactly the same blind spot
as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing. It would also break this
organism's own stated design principle ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal
state," `index.tsx` ~349-350) and introduce real SSR/hydration-mismatch risk pure CSS structurally
can't have, for no correctness gain.

**Why this doesn't reintroduce the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when*
`:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus
moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property
the matched rule sets. The trigger selectors aren't touched at all; only the property values
inside the already-existing blocks change.

**Docblock updates:** extend/rewrite docblock points 3 and 6 and the "Fix H" note with a new dated
fix note (continuing the lettered sequence), stating explicitly that Fix H's `:focus-within` →
`:has(:focus-visible)` swap was and remains correct for the paint-timing question it solved, and
that the actual defect was using `display` (an AT-tree-removal property) to answer a different
question than the one it should answer. Explicitly out of scope, left as `display:none`: the
permanent, non-hover-capable-pointer hides (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s unconditional size-chip
hide, the PLP-mobile bag-icon hide) — separate, correct, Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions,
since nothing about them is gated behind an interaction heuristic.

**Test updates:** the existing `.matches()`-based selector-proof describe block in
`index.test.tsx` needs no change (it doesn't depend on which property the matched rule sets). Any
structural/object-shape assertions elsewhere in the same file checking the recipe's declared
`display` values for these 5 sites need updating to the new property values — identify the exact
assertions at implementation time against the real current file, don't guess line numbers here.

**New real-browser verification** (jsdom can't prove any of this): this repo already has
scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js`'s `a11y-desktop` →
`e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`, `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`; both Chromium-only, no WebKit
project configured — not touching `playwright.config.js` itself, only adding specs inside the
already-existing target directories). Add specs for:

1. **Accessibility-tree presence** — load a card in its default (non-hovered, non-focused) state
   and assert, via a real Chromium accessibility-tree snapshot, that the size-chip radiogroup,
   notify-me button, and carousel arrow buttons are present with correct role/name — proving
   AT-tree presence no longer depends on any hover/focus-visible condition having matched.
2. **Tab-order parity** — forward-Tab from before the card and Shift+Tab from after it, asserting
   the stop set/sequence is now identical in both directions (today Shift+Tab skips the
   reveal-gated controls entirely).
3. **No regression on the original stuck-open bug** — real mouse click on an arrow button, move
   the mouse off the card, assert the control is no longer visually painted by reading
   `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath` directly (Playwright's default `toBeVisible()` is primarily a
   bounding-box/`visibility` check and may not reliably catch clip-path-based hiding).

**Honest limitation, not skippable:** the actual disputed claim — does real VoiceOver announce and
activate these controls — can't be fully closed out by any automated check above. Chromium's
accessibility tree isn't the engine VoiceOver actually talks to (WebKit), no WebKit Playwright
project exists in this repo, and Playwright can't drive real VoiceOver at all. The automated specs
give strong, real regression-prevention signal (AT-tree presence + tab-order parity are both real,
previously-uncaught bugs), but final confirmation needs one manual pass from Marcel: navigate a
card via VO+Right-Arrow/rotor only (no mouse, no literal Tab keypress) on real macOS Safari +
VoiceOver, confirming price, the size-chip radiogroup, notify-me, and the carousel arrows are all
announced and activatable via VO+Space.

## Verification (both fixes)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full local Storybook build + `test-storybook --ci` — same pattern used earlier on this branch
   for the axe-contrast fix; confirms no regression across the whole story set.
3. Updated/new Vitest assertions in both `index.test.tsx` files pass.
4. New Playwright a11y specs (AT-tree presence, tab-order parity, stuck-open non-regression) pass.
5. Real-device/manual checks, both required before calling this done:
   - Real touch swipe (device or Playwright mobile-chrome touch simulation) confirms gallery
     paging works, a plain tap still navigates to the PDP, and the arrow/remove buttons still do
     only their own thing (no accidental navigation).
   - Real VoiceOver + Safari pass (Marcel, one-time) confirms AT reachability/activation for all
     five previously-broken controls.

## Files touched

All within one protection tier — squad-owned `ui-kits` component recipes/tests, no Tier 1/2 file:

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` (new click-passthrough
  handler, exact placement decided at implementation time)
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` (only if the
  carousel base-state change needs an assertion update there too — confirm at implementation time)
- New: `e2e/tests/a11y/desktop/*.spec.ts`, `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile/*.spec.ts` (exact filenames
  follow this repo's existing spec-naming convention, decided at implementation time)

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPostBuild

Marcel's own senior dev. Nothing built here — this skill judges what was built, writes what goes
public, and holds the conversation with CodeRabbit and the reviewer.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Input:** `Final wrap-up pass for SFCC-236 (Product Card Shared Component) before opening the PR. HEAD is now at 4740dd5, 5 commits past Round 9's last audit (72ee2a9 arrows hover-gating fix, 983bddf :has(:focus-visible) stuck-open-hover fix, 0748af3 was/now sale price story for ProductCardContent, 02a3203 ZimmProductCard stories consolidation — nodeCoverage/ deleted, 11 stories in one file, 4740dd5 slide-indicator docblock clarification). Explicit checks requested by the developer for this round:
- Check against the build plan (~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md) — confirm the shipped state still matches, flag any drift.
- Check the JIRA ticket (SFCC-236) details, ACs, and comment thread directly — not just prior session summaries of them.
- Check the designs: design spec accuracy, tokens, etc., via the live Figma design nodes (not cached descriptions).
- Run visual checks (Storybook, real rendering).
- Run accessibility checks (keyboard nav, screen reader/ARIA correctness, WCAG 2.2 AA per AGENTS.md).
This is intended to be the final round before the PR is opened — treat it as a genuinely fresh, thorough audit, not a diff-only check of the 5 recent commits.` — a Jira key. Reads three files under
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- **`handoff.md`** — Build's record: steps, commits, Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers,
  UNIFORM findings, what went unverified
- **`plan.md`** — what was meant to be built
- **`findings.md`** — the gate table, with its 🟡 CLARIFY assumptions

If `handoff.md` is missing, Build either did not finish or ran before this was written. Say so and
reconstruct what you can from the branch's commits — but flag the audit as partial, because the
Scorer verdicts and UNIFORM findings are not recoverable from git.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get a five-agent sweep. Honour the scale the
plan chose. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — audit against both artefacts

Two documents, two different questions. Neither is covered by the loop that just ran.

### `findings.md` — did the gate hold?

Walk every row. For each:

- **🔴 BLOCKED** — was it resolved before Build started, and by what?
- **🟡 CLARIFY** — this is the one that matters. Each of these carried a **stated assumption** into
  the plan. **Did that assumption actually hold once the code existed?** Nothing else in the chain
  revisits them. An assumption that turned out wrong mid-build, that nobody went back to, is the
  most likely thing to reach the PR unnoticed.
- **🔵 NOTE** — still true? A note that has become a defect is a finding.

### `plan.md` — did the build deliver?

- Every step shipped what it promised, with its Scorer verdict.
- The diff matches the file manifest. Anything in the diff that isn't in the manifest is a scope
  finding — even if it looks correct.
- Every file's tier is what the plan said it was.
- **Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.** Never a finding.

Use `zm-orchestrator` for the manifest-versus-diff conformance pass. It already does exactly this
judgement at step scope.

---

## Phase 2 — the whole-feature sweep

Per-step scoring is **structurally blind** to a pattern applied consistently but wrongly: it
passes every individual review. On this project a systematic spacing error survived five commits
and every score, and was only found afterwards. This phase exists for that.

Run it in two directions, internal first.

### Internal — does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric. One question: is this internally consistent?

- Every recipe the same shape — same `parts` convention, same registration, same naming
- Every component the same structure — export, props type, story, test
- Every token used the same way for the same purpose
- The same value not typed twice in two places

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible.

### External — does that shared shape conform?

Only once you know what the feature's own pattern *is*:

- **The exemplar PR** — does the feature match what it established? Where the exemplar is itself
  inconsistent, say which variant this work followed and whether that was the better choice. Do
  not report a divergence from an unstable pattern as a defect.
- **`.claude/rules/*`** — do the rules hold across the whole feature, not just per file?
- **Figma, end to end** — the rendered feature against the named nodes, every variant and state.
  Remember the node-type discriminator and never cross-compare the two Figma files.

Use `zm-tester` for this, fanning out across the feature rather than one step. Every finding
carries **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — at this scope, UNIFORM is what you are hunting.

---

## Phase 3 — if the audit fails

**Hand back to `zimmerMANNBuild`. Do not fix it here.**

The auditor becoming the author is exactly the independence that makes this phase worth running,
and Build has a Scorer and a rework cap that this skill does not.

Report the defect with its evidence, return the work, and **re-audit when it comes back.** A
re-audit is a fresh pass, not a check that the named item changed.

---

## Phase 4 — the PR

Write the body yourself. Do not call `/pr-checklist` — its output is the team's format, and this
one is yours.

**The body describes the diff that actually shipped, not the plan.** If the two differ, the diff
wins and the difference is worth a line.

Include: what changed and why · the tier of every touched file, with any Tier 2 approver named ·
what was tested and the real numbers · anything deliberately deferred, with the owning ticket ·
anything left unverified.

**Never in a PR title, body, commit message or code comment:**
- Claude attribution of any kind — no `Co-Authored-By`, no mention
- CodeRabbit mentions
- A citation of any local-only doc. `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are Marcel's
  personal files. Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite that.
- Draft or pending disclaimers

Match the house standard by reading Marcel's own previously authored PRs on this repo, not by
inferring a format.

---

## Phase 5 — write it down, then present

**First write `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md`:**

```
# PostBuild — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Head: <sha>   Audited: <date>

## Audit — findings.md
| # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence |
<one row per row of findings.md. For every 🟡 CLARIFY: did the assumption hold?>

## Audit — plan.md
| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
<plus: files in the diff that were not in the manifest>

## Sweep — internal consistency
<does the feature agree with itself — recipes, structure, token use>

## Sweep — external conformance
<exemplar PR · .claude/rules/* · Figma end to end>

## UNIFORM findings
<the ones a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## PR body as written
<the exact text>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>
```

**Then append a block per review round**, as the loop runs:

```
## Round <n> — <date>
Findings received: <n> (CodeRabbit <n>, reviewer <n>)
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
<VALID / INVALID / OUT OF SCOPE / DEFER, with the evidence for each decline>
```

This file is read by **`zimmerMANNBuild rework`** — so it knows what was already declined and why,
rather than re-litigating it — and by **`zimmerMANNDevImprover`**. Write it even when the audit is
clean; a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Then present

Give him, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register:

1. The diff summary — files, tiers, commits
2. The audit result — every gate item and plan step, with anything that failed
3. The sweep result — **UNIFORM findings first**, they are the point of this skill
4. The proposed PR title and body
5. What could not be verified

Then **stop.**

**On his go: push and open the PR.** Not before. Push is the first irreversible, outward-facing
step in the chain, and it is his to authorise.

---

## Phase 6 — the review loop

When CodeRabbit or a reviewer requests changes:

1. **Hand the findings to `zimmerMANNBuild rework`.** It verifies each finding is real before
   anything is touched — CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo — then fixes and
   commits the valid ones.

2. **Draft a reply for every finding when it comes back.** Every thread gets a written answer:
   - **Fixed** — what changed, and the commit
   - **Declined** — the specific quotable repo rule, doc, or empirical result that makes it wrong.
     Not an opinion.
   - **Deferred** — the owning ticket or the person who decides

   **A fix commit with no in-thread reply does not count.** A prior PR here carried 18 threads with
   zero human replies; the process was being followed on the PR before it and was dropped entirely.

3. **Show him the full batch, then post on his go.** One approval covers the set.

4. Repeat until approved. If CodeRabbit raises the same objection a third time, stop re-running it
   and answer the threads instead — it has nothing to learn from unanswered comments.

**Before final hand-off, re-run the manifest check — not just once, at the end.** Phase 2's
manifest-versus-diff audit is a snapshot, not a standing guarantee. Any fix round in this phase
(a CodeRabbit rework, a reviewer's requested change, or a gap Marcel spots and Build fixes
directly) can add a file outside the original manifest — including a legitimate, individually-
authorized Tier 1/2 exception. If it does, that file belongs in the plan's manifest and in
postbuild.md's own audit paragraph, not left for the audit to silently go stale. Before presenting
the final state for merge, confirm the manifest audit's claim still matches `git diff
<base>..HEAD --numstat` exactly — if it doesn't, append a dated correction (same pattern as
plan.md's own "Open questions" section) rather than leaving the original claim uncorrected.

---

## The owner rule — everywhere outward-facing

The audit report, the PR body, and every reply.

Every finding names **who resolves it**: Marcel, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA. A blocker owned by the
designer and one owned by Marcel need different actions.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question to them — never a directive.**
"Should this route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before anything posts, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as
hiding behind their authority.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** Every fix goes back to Build. This skill audits, writes, and posts.
- **Never push or post without an explicit go.** Both are outward-facing and irreversible in
  practice.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never re-litigate a settled decision.** If the plan decided it and the build honoured it, it
  is not a finding — report a *mechanical consequence* of a decision, never the decision.
- **Say what you could not verify.** An audit that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

content.text: Found both threads — comment `3939994904` (modifier-click, `index.tsx:473`) and `3939994913` (touch size-selector, `zimmProductCard.css.ts:411`). Writing the reply bodies to files to avoid shell-escaping issues with the nested quotes, then posting both as in-thread replies.

input.content: Good catch, verified and fixed in `79384ad`. `handleMediaClick` now bails out on `event.metaKey`/`ctrlKey`/`shiftKey`/`altKey` or a non-primary button, so a modifier-click or middle-click no longer forces an in-tab `history.push` — it falls through and does nothing instead, same as it would if the click had landed outside the card. That's not quite full parity with a real `<a>` (it doesn't open a new tab the way native anchor semantics would), but it's the right tradeoff here: not silently overriding an explicit "open elsewhere" signal matters more than replicating the exact browser chrome behavior, and going further (e.g. `window.open`) felt like scope creep for what this handler actually needs to guarantee. Added `test.each`-based coverage for all five cases (Cmd, Ctrl, Shift, Alt, non-primary button) so this can't silently regress again.

input.content: Confirmed and fixed in `79384ad` — and it turned out to be a slightly bigger fix than just this one spot. You're right that the unconditional `clip-path` here left the size-selector permanently tabbable-but-invisible on touch, since `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` never matches there and there's no other reveal path. Went with your first option (scope the hidden state to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, `display:none` for the rest) rather than making it visible-by-default on touch — that would've been a real change to the confirmed Figma/PLP design (size picker is intentionally a hover-capable-only affordance), not just a technical fix. While tracing the mechanism I found the exact same issue on the carousel arrows too (same unconditional-clip-path-with-no-touch-reveal-path shape) — fixed that alongside it. Verified live against both device profiles: desktop still reveals both correctly on hover/focus, and touch's forward-tab sequence no longer lands on either control at all.

+ * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
+ * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
+ * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
+ * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
+ * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
+ * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
+ * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
+ * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
+ * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
+ * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
+ * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
+ * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
+ * rather than silently picked.
+ *
+ * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
+ * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
+ * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
+ * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
+ * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
+ * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
+ * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
+ * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
+ * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
+ * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
+ *
+ * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
+ * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
+ * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
+ * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
+ * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
+ * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
+ * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
+ * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
+ * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
+ * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
+ *
+ * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
+ * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
+ * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
+ * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
+ * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
+ * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
+ * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
+ * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
+ * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
+ * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
+ * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
+ * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
+ *
+ * Fix I (SFCC-236, found via live mobile-device testing on this branch, same round that found
+ * Fix H): multi-image cards did not respond to a real touch swipe at all — the slide indicator
+ * rendered correctly (so the image data/gallery logic was fine), but swiping the image never
+ * paged it. Root cause and CSS fix are `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own Fix I (docblock point 2):
+ * `ZimmProductCardMedia` was the one interactive region never lifted above the stretched-link
+ * overlay, so a swipe gesture starting on the image landed on the invisible overlay `<a>` first
+ * and never reached the real scroll container underneath. Lifting Media above the overlay fixes
+ * the swipe, but has a side effect: a plain tap/click on the image used to "work" by landing on
+ * that same overlay and navigating to the PDP — once Media sits on top, the tap no longer reaches
+ * it, and Media itself had no click behaviour of its own. `handleMediaClick` below restores that
+ * navigation deliberately, via `useHistory().push(href)` rather than depending on the overlay by
+ * accident: this repo is pinned to react-router-dom v5.3.4 (`package.json`), which has no
+ * `useNavigate` — `useHistory()` + `history.push()` is the correct v5 primitive, already
+ * established in this codebase (`footer/index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`,
+ * `pages/product-detail/index.tsx`) and the same one the base SFCC `product-list` page itself
+ * uses. `href` needed no new prop plumbing — this organism already destructures it from its own
+ * base props (above) and previously only forwarded it to `ZimmProductCardContent`. The handler
+ * guards against the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button — all real `<button>`
+ * descendants of `ZimmProductCardMedia` — via `(event.target as HTMLElement).closest('button')`,
+ * so paging and `onRemove` keep firing on their own and never also navigate. No custom drag-vs-tap
+ * detection is needed for the swipe/tap split itself: browsers natively suppress the synthetic
+ * `click` event after a real drag/scroll on the same element, so a swipe pages the gallery without
+ * ever reaching this handler, while a plain tap (no movement) still fires it exactly as the old
+ * overlay click did.
+ */
+
+/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
+ *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
+ *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
+export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;
+
+/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
+ *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
+ *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
+type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];
+
+/**
+ * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
+ * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
+ * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
+ * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
+ * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
+ * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
+ * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
+ * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
+ * `buildCardProps` helper.
+ */
+export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
+  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
+   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
+   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
+   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
+  id: string;
+  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
+   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
+  href: string;
+  name: string;
+  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
+  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
+  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
+  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
+  currentPrice?: string;
+  originalPrice?: string;
+  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
+  isUnavailable?: boolean;
+  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
+   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
+  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
+  /**
+   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
+   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
+   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
+   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
+   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
+   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
+   */
+  badge?: string;
+};
+
+export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
+  variation: 'plp';
+  onAddToBag?: () => void;
+  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
+  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
+  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
+};
+
+export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
+  variation: 'home';
+  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
+};
+
+export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
+  variation: 'wishlist';
+  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
+  colour: string;
+  size: string;
+  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
+  onRemove: () => void;
+  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
+  onAddToBag?: () => void;
+  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
+   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
+   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
+   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
+   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
+   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
+   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
+  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
+  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
+  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
+};
+
+export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
+  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);
+
+type ZimmProductCardVariation =
+  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
+  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
+  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];
+
+/**
+ * Widened, not narrowed: every variation-specific field is optional here regardless of which
+ * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
+ * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
+ * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
+ * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
+ * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
+ * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
+ * about what a caller may legally pass in.
+ */
+type ZimmProductCardVariationFields = Partial<
+  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
+    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
+    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
+>;
+
+type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
+  showBag: boolean;
+  showAttributes: boolean;
+  showSizeChips: boolean;
+  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
+  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
+  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
+  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
+  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
+  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
+  showRemove: boolean;
+  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
+   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
+   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
+   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
+  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
+  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
+   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
+   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
+   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
+   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
+   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
+   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
+  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
+  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
+  showBadge: boolean;
+  /**
+   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
+   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
+   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
+   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
+   */
+  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
+};
+
+/**
+ * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
+ * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
+ * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
+ * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
+ * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
+ */
+const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
+  home: {
+    showBag: false,
+    showAttributes: false,
+    showSizeChips: false,
+    hoverHidesPrice: false,
+    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
+    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
+    showRemove: false,
+    hideBagOnMobile: false,
+    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
+    showBadge: false,
+    showHoverImageSwap: false,
+  },
+  plp: {
+    showBag: true,
+    showAttributes: false,
+    showSizeChips: true,
+    hoverHidesPrice: true,
+    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
+    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
+    showRemove: false,
+    hideBagOnMobile: true,
+    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
+    showBadge: true,
+    showHoverImageSwap: true,
+  },
+  wishlist: {
+    showBag: true,
+    showAttributes: true,
+    showSizeChips: true,
+    hoverHidesPrice: true,
+    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
+    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
+    showRemove: true,
+    hideBagOnMobile: false,
+    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
+    showBadge: true,
+    showHoverImageSwap: true,
+  },
+};
+
+const messages = defineMessages({
+  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
+  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
+  // site that actually knows the product name.
+  removeFromWishlist: {
+    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
+    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
+  },
+});
+
+const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';
+
+/**
+ * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
+ * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
+ * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
+ * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
+ * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
+ * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
+ *
+ * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
+ */
+export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
+  const {
+    id,
+    href,
+    name,
+    headingLevel,
+    primaryImage,
+    hoverImage,
+    images,
+    currentPrice,
+    originalPrice,
+    isPriceLoading,
+    isUnavailable,
+    onNotifyMe,
+    badge,
+    variation,
+  } = props;
+
+  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
+    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;
+
+  const intl = useIntl();
+  const history = useHistory();
+  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];
+
+  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
+  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
+  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
+  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
+
+  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
+  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
+  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
+  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
+  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
+  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
+  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
+  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
+  //
+  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
+  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
+  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
+  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
+  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
+  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
+  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
+  //
+  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
+  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
+  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
+  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
+  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
+  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
+  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
+  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
+  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
+  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
+  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
+
+  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
+  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
+  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
+  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
+  // not why.
+  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));
+
+  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
+  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;
+
+  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
+    hoverHidesPrice,
+    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
+    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
+    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
+    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
+    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
+    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
+    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
+    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
+    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
+    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
+    // mounted at all.
+    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
+    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
+  });
+
+  // Fix I — see the module docblock's own "Fix I" paragraph for the full narrative. Guards the
+  //
